On geometry, the updates are numerically full-rank but spectrally concentrated; they lie mostly away from the principal singular subspaces of the source weights and fall disproportionately on coordinates where the source weights are close to zero. These findings suggest that dense teacher supervision does not turn \textsc{OPD} into ordinary dense parameter rewriting; instead, \textsc{OPD} retains important geometric signatures of on-policy post-training.

AI.tldr: On-policy distillation (OPD) uses sparse, effective updates across model layers and retains key geometric signatures of on-policy tuning, with dense teacher supervision influencing performance.
AI.motivation: The paper investigates how on-policy distillation (OPD) affects model parameters during post-training, combining on-policy trajectories with teacher supervision.
AI.method: The authors analyze updates across various language and vision-language models, focusing on their sparsity and geometric characteristics.
AI.result: Findings indicate that OPD updates are small, coordinate-sparse, and concentrated away from significant singular subspaces, with a notable performance recovery from subnetwork training.
AI.conclusion: The presence of dense teacher supervision in OPD preserves geometric features from on-policy training and diverges from typical dense parameter adjustments.

title: The Stable Recovery Manifold: Geometric Principles Governing Recoverability in Continual Learning
summary: Catastrophic forgetting is often viewed as the destruction of previously learned knowledge during sequential learning. Building on the Accessibility Collapse framework, we investigate the geometric structure of recoverability in continual learning. Using Split CIFAR-100 and a sequentially trained ResNet-18, we analyze recoverability, representational drift, and recovery complexity across ten tasks. We introduce Recovery Subspace Dimensionality (k_t), a measure of the minimum number of singular directions required to preserve 90 percent of full probe performance. Contrary to our Recoverability Diffusion hypothesis, recovery dimensionality remains stable throughout training (mean k_t = 8.0) despite substantial representational drift. Principal-angle drift strongly predicts recoverability (r = -0.862), and a simple geometric model explains 82.2 percent of recoverability variance. These findings support the Stable Recovery Manifold hypothesis, suggesting that forgotten knowledge remains compactly decodable despite representational reorganization. The results indicate that catastrophic forgetting is primarily an accessibility and manifold-alignment problem rather than information destruction.

AI.tldr: The study investigates catastrophic forgetting in continual learning using geometric analysis of recoverability and introduces a new measure, Recovery Subspace Dimensionality, revealing that recovery dimensionality remains stable despite representational drift, suggesting that forgetting is more about accessibility than the loss of information.
AI.motivation: To understand catastrophic forgetting not as a destruction of knowledge but as an issue of accessibility and manifold alignment in continual learning tasks.
AI.method: Analyzed recoverability, representational drift, and recovery complexity in a sequentially trained ResNet-18 on Split CIFAR-100 across ten tasks, introducing Recovery Subspace Dimensionality (k_t).
AI.result: Recovery dimensionality (mean k_t = 8.0) was stable despite representational drift; principal-angle drift was a strong predictor of recoverability, explaining 82.2% of its variance.
AI.conclusion: Catastrophic forgetting is better characterized as an issue of accessibility and manifold alignment rather than mere information destruction, supported by the Stable Recovery Manifold hypothesis.

title: Understanding Truncated Positional Encodings for Graph Neural Networks
summary: Positional encodings (PEs) enhance the power of graph neural networks (GNNs), both theoretically and empirically. Two of the most popular families of PEs - spectral (e.g., Laplacian eigenspaces, effective resistance) and walk-based (polynomials of the adjacency matrix) - are theoretically equivalent in expressive power, with expressivity between the 1-WL and 3-WL tests. However, this equivalence assumes the GNN uses the "complete" version of these PEs, which requires $O(n^3)$ time and space complexity. Instead, practitioners commonly use truncated variants of these encodings, such as the first $k$ eigenspaces or powers of the adjacency matrix. However, the theoretical properties of these truncated PEs are unknown. In this work, we initiate the study of these truncated PEs. Theoretically, we show that, under truncation, several families of PEs are fundamentally different in expressive power. As a corollary, we show that truncated spectral PEs are no longer stronger than the 1-WL test. We also study a family of spectral PEs, the $k$-harmonic distances, to highlight the differences in expressive power of even closely related truncated PEs. Finally, we experimentally show that a mix of truncated PEs is preferable to any single family on real-world datasets.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes the expressive power of truncated positional encodings (PEs) in graph neural networks (GNNs), revealing that their theoretical properties differ significantly, especially showing that truncated spectral PEs are not more expressive than the 1-WL test.
AI.motivation: Understanding the effectiveness of truncated positional encodings in GNNs, as existing knowledge is primarily based on complete PEs, which are computationally intensive.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of truncated PEs' expressive powers and experimental validation on real-world datasets to compare the performance of mixed truncated PEs to single family variants.
AI.result: Truncated positional encodings exhibit fundamentally different expressive powers compared to complete PEs, with findings indicating that truncated spectral PEs have limited strength similar to the 1-WL test.
AI.conclusion: A mix of truncated PEs is more effective on real-world datasets than relying on any single family of PEs.
